good_sentence: This book is easy to read.
bad_sentence: This book is eager to read.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: 'Easy' is a tough-adjective allowing the object gap (read this book); 'eager' is an eager-class adjective that forces a subject-control reading, which is anomalous for an inanimate subject.

good_sentence: The puzzle is hard to solve.
bad_sentence: The puzzle is hard to solve it.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: Tough-movement requires an object gap after the infinitive; filling the object with 'it' is ungrammatical.

good_sentence: These instructions are simple to follow.
bad_sentence: These instructions are reluctant to follow.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: 'Simple' licenses the object gap; 'reluctant' is an eager-class predicate requiring an agentive subject, so the object-gap reading is unavailable.

good_sentence: The melody was pleasant to hear.
bad_sentence: The melody was pleasant to hear it.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: The infinitive must contain an object gap coindexed with the subject; the resumptive 'it' fills the gap and is ungrammatical.

good_sentence: That argument is difficult to refute.
bad_sentence: That argument is keen to refute.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: 'Difficult' is a tough-predicate; 'keen' is eager-class and demands a willing subject, which an abstract argument cannot be.

good_sentence: The contract is impossible to break.
bad_sentence: The contract is impossible to break it.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: A gap is obligatory after 'break'; inserting the pronoun 'it' as object violates tough-movement.

good_sentence: The lecture was tough to follow.
bad_sentence: The lecture was anxious to follow.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: 'Tough' allows object extraction; 'anxious' is an eager-class adjective whose subject must be a sentient experiencer, ruling out the object-gap reading.

good_sentence: Her handwriting is hard to decipher.
bad_sentence: Her handwriting is hard to decipher it.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: The object position after 'decipher' must be a gap; the resumptive pronoun 'it' is ungrammatical.

good_sentence: This recipe is easy to prepare.
bad_sentence: This recipe is willing to prepare.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: 'Easy' is a tough-adjective; 'willing' is eager-class and requires a volitional subject, so the inanimate-subject object-gap reading fails.

good_sentence: The trail is pleasant to walk.
bad_sentence: The trail is pleasant to walk it.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: Tough-movement leaves an object gap after 'walk'; filling it with 'it' is ungrammatical.

good_sentence: The code is tricky to debug.
bad_sentence: The code is hesitant to debug.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: 'Tricky' patterns as a tough-predicate; 'hesitant' is eager-class, requiring an agentive subject, so the object-gap reading is unavailable.

good_sentence: The wine was delightful to taste.
bad_sentence: The wine was delightful to taste it.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: The infinitival object must be gapped; the overt pronoun 'it' double-fills the position and is ungrammatical.

good_sentence: The form is annoying to fill out.
bad_sentence: The form is determined to fill out.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: 'Annoying' allows object extraction; 'determined' is eager-class and selects a sentient, intentional subject, so the form-as-object reading collapses.

good_sentence: This knot is impossible to untie.
bad_sentence: This knot is impossible to untie it.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: The object slot after 'untie' must remain a gap; the resumptive 'it' violates tough-movement.

good_sentence: The poem is lovely to recite.
bad_sentence: The poem is curious to recite.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: 'Lovely' is a tough-predicate licensing the gap; 'curious' (in the eager sense) needs an animate experiencer subject, so the object-gap reading is anomalous.

good_sentence: The machine is dangerous to operate.
bad_sentence: The machine is dangerous to operate it.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: Tough-movement requires the object of 'operate' to be a gap; adding 'it' is ungrammatical.

good_sentence: His accent is difficult to imitate.
bad_sentence: His accent is proud to imitate.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: 'Difficult' allows the object gap; 'proud' is eager-class and predicates an emotional state of a sentient subject, so the accent-as-object reading fails.

good_sentence: The river is safe to cross here.
bad_sentence: The river is safe to cross it here.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: The object of 'cross' must be gapped; the pronoun 'it' fills the gap and renders the sentence ungrammatical.

good_sentence: The theorem is hard to prove.
bad_sentence: The theorem is ready to prove.
source: author-constructed (template, cf. SyntaxGym; Hu et al. 2020)
notes: 'Hard' is a tough-adjective; 'ready' is eager-class, so 'the theorem is ready to prove' forces a subject-as-prover reading, which is anomalous.

good_sentence: That dress is expensive to clean.
bad_sentence: That dress is expensive to clean it.

good_sentence: The song is fun to sing.

good_sentence: This sauce is quick to make.

good_sentence: The story is enjoyable to retell.
bad_sentence: The story is impatient to retell.

good_sentence: The map is confusing to interpret.

good_sentence: Her point was awkward to address.

good_sentence: The fabric is delicate to handle.

good_sentence: The dialect is interesting to study.
bad_sentence: The dialect is eager to study.

good_sentence: This question is tough to answer.

good_sentence: The bridge is scary to drive across.

good_sentence: The data are easy to misread.
